title: The Aronde 1300 Oceane line: the styling details that really matter
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: In 1956, the Oceane line gives the Aronde a more assertive tone. The restyle matters less as gratuitous effect than as a way of keeping the car credible against competition that is modernising quickly.
content:
The Oceane line remains one of the keywords of the Aronde 1300. To understand what it changes, however, one has to look beyond the formula and return to volumes, front end and the car’s overall balance.

A calculated modernisation

In 1956 Simca does not remake the Aronde from top to bottom. The marque instead reworks the visual reading so the car sits inside a newer climate of style, with a measured yet visible American influence.

The Oceane line fulfils exactly that function: show that the car follows its time without breaking with its original structure.

What to look at on the car

The grille, rear end, roof volumes and certain presentation details tell the Oceane story better than any single badge or label. It is a whole attitude of style rather than a mere ornament.

That nuance matters greatly for identifying an example or judging the coherence of a restoration.

Why the Oceane line remains so memorable

The Aronde 1300 finds one of its best balance points here. It remains recognisable as an Aronde, yet looks more dressed and more self-assured.

That may explain why many enthusiasts remember this phase as one of the line’s most accurate, between the beginnings of the Simca 9 and the more demonstrative P60.
